title: Invalidate-don't-delete pattern for retiring constraints
context: Constraints had no CLI retirement path; hand-editing JSON was the only way. Decisions already used invalidate-don't-delete via supersede, preserving history while stopping active surfacing. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex).
decision: retire-constraint command sets status='retired' and valid_to=now instead of deleting, mirroring the decision supersede pattern. Idempotent-refuse (error on nonexistent or already-retired) rather than silent no-op.
consequences: Retired constraints remain queryable in full history (not destructively removed)
Expired constraints stop appearing in active views (Top invariants, hunch check) but audit trail persists
Consistent invalidation semantics across decisions and constraints
CLI rejects redundant retire attempts with explicit error, making user intent visible
alternatives_rejected: Destructively delete constraint records (loses audit trail and history)
Silent idempotent no-op on already-retired constraints (obscures accidental double-retirement)
